import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Hermitian
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Star
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# The determinant family's single-block precision

Literal equation (4) and the single-block argument of Appendix B.3,
equation (26), in Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
The full block-diagonal construction and unique minimizer are separate obligations.
-/

open Matrix

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

/-- The literal single-block precision in source equation (4). -/
noncomputable def singleBlockPrecision {n : ℕ} (κ : ℝ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
  ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) -
    ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) +
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)

/-- Appendix B.3, equation (26), retaining the source's standing n and κ range. -/
theorem singleBlockPrecision_regular {n : ℕ} (_hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    (singleBlockPrecision κ O).IsHermitian ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n → ℝ,
        v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ v ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ v) ∧
        v ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ v) ≤ κ * (v ⬝ᵥ v) := by
  constructor
  · rw [Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSymm]
    unfold Matrix.IsSymm singleBlockPrecision
    simp only [Matrix.transpose_sub, Matrix.transpose_smul, Matrix.transpose_one,
      Matrix.transpose_add, Matrix.transpose_transpose]
    rw [add_comm (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose]
  · intro v
    have horth : (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) = 1 :=
      (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff' (Fin n) ℝ).mp O.property
    have hiso : ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ
        ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) = v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      rw [dotProduct_comm, ← Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec,
        Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, horth, Matrix.one_mulVec]
    have hq : 0 ≤ v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      exact Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => mul_self_nonneg (v i))
    have hcs : (v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)) ^ 2 ≤
        (v ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2 := by
      have h := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ v
        ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)
      simp only [pow_two] at h ⊢
      change (v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)) *
          (v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)) ≤
        (v ⬝ᵥ v) * (((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ
          ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)) at h
      rw [hiso] at h
      exact h
    have hcross : -(v ⬝ᵥ v) ≤ v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) ∧
        v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) ≤ v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      constructor <;> nlinarith
    have htranspose : v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *ᵥ v) =
        v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v) :=
      Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec _ _ _
    have hexpand : v ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ v) =
        ((κ + 1) / 2) * (v ⬝ᵥ v) -
          ((κ - 1) / 2) * (v ⬝ᵥ ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ v)) := by
      simp only [singleBlockPrecision, Matrix.sub_mulVec, Matrix.smul_mulVec,
        Matrix.add_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec, dotProduct_sub, dotProduct_smul,
        dotProduct_add, htranspose, smul_eq_mul]
      ring
    have hc : 0 ≤ (κ - 1) / 2 := by linarith
    have hlow := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcross.2 hc
    have hupp := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcross.1 hc
    rw [hexpand]
    constructor <;> nlinarith

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

lesson.statement: Let n>=3, kappa>=4 and O belong to the real orthogonal group O(n). The matrix A_O in equation (4) is real symmetric, and every real vector v satisfies v^T v <= v^T A_O v <= kappa v^T v. This is the quadratic-form formulation of source equation (26).

steps.title: Orthogonality preserves the Euclidean squared norm
steps.text: Use O^T O=I to reduce (Ov)^T(Ov) to v^T v. Squared Euclidean norms are represented by sums of squared coordinates.
steps.lean: horth uses Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff'; hiso uses the transpose dot-product identity and matrix multiplication.

steps.title: Control the cross term
steps.text: Finite-sum Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the square of the cross term. Together with v^T v>=0 this gives both signed inequalities. These estimates are derived inside the proof.
steps.lean: hcs applies Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq; hcross derives the two real bounds.

steps.title: Expand the quadratic form
steps.text: Over the reals, v^T O^T v equals v^T O v, so the two transpose cross terms combine.
steps.lean: htranspose is Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec; hexpand distributes mulVec and dotProduct and checks the coefficient algebra.

steps.title: Scale with the correct sign and prove symmetry
steps.text: The standing kappa>=4 implies (kappa-1)/2>=0. Substituting the upper and lower cross-term bounds gives the lower and upper quadratic bounds respectively. Transpose fixes both I and O+O^T, hence A_O is symmetric.
steps.lean: hc discharges the sign from hκ. hlow/hupp scale hcross. The first conjunction proves real Hermitianity, equivalently symmetry.

lesson.lean_statement: The statement uses IsHermitian over ℝ and explicit universal dot-product inequalities, avoiding entrywise matrix order and the default Pi norm.
lesson.lean_proof: The checked proof follows the source orthogonality → Cauchy–Schwarz → quadratic expansion route.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n with n >= 3, every real number kappa with kappa >= 4, and every real orthogonal n by n matrix O, let A = ((kappa + 1)/2) I_n - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T). Then A is symmetric (A = A^T), and for every vector v in R^n, ||v||_2^2 <= v^T A v <= kappa ||v||_2^2. The same matrix A satisfies both inequalities for every vector v, including the zero vector.
